# Add Audio to Video

- Route: `/tools/stitch-audio-to-video`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `video`
- Slug: `stitch-audio-to-video`

## Summary

Combine a base video with up to three additional audio files — voiceovers, music, narration — and download a new MP4. (Video tools)

## Details

Combining a base video with one or more additional audio files is one of the most common editing tasks — adding a voiceover, dropping in a backing track, narrating a screen recording, or replacing the original audio entirely. Media Manipulator gives you per-track volume and offset controls, a mix-vs-replace toggle, and an MP4 output that drops cleanly into any player.
### What it does
- Combines a base video with up to three additional audio tracks.
- Per-track controls: volume (0–4×), start offset in seconds, optional loop-to-video-length.
- Top-level mode toggle: "mix" keeps the original audio, "replace" drops it.
- Output is always MP4 with AAC audio at 192 kbps — the safe everywhere default.
### How to use it
1. Upload the base video: Drop any MP4, MOV, MKV, WebM, AVI, or M4V file.
2. Add audio tracks: Add up to three audio files (voiceover, music, narration) with per-track settings.
3. Pick mix or replace: Keep the original audio and mix in the new tracks, or drop the original and use only the new audio.
4. Download the new MP4: We stitch on our server and return a clean MP4.
### Supported formats
- Input: mp4, mov, webm, mkv, avi, m4v (video), mp3, wav, m4a, aac, flac, ogg (audio)
- Output: mp4
- Video stream is stream-copied where possible — only audio is re-encoded (to AAC 192 kbps).
- Loop checkbox extends short backing tracks to the video length.
### Technical details
- The filter graph is built programmatically: per-track adelay + volume nodes, then a single amix to combine them.
- The video stream is stream-copied wherever possible — only the audio is re-encoded (to AAC at 192 kbps).
- Looping is implemented with `-stream_loop -1` on the audio input so short backing tracks extend to the video duration cleanly.
- Output duration is "trim to video duration" by default — uncheck if you want the output to extend to the longest input.
### Use cases
- Creator videos: Add a music bed under a talking-head segment, or replace the room audio with a clean voiceover.
- Tutorials: Drop a narration track on top of a screen recording.
- Social clips: Add a trending track at a specific offset to a 15-second cut.
- Family / personal videos: Add background music to a vacation montage.
### FAQ
Q: Can I add music to a video?
A: Yes — add the music file as an audio track, set its volume, and leave the mode on "mix" to keep the original audio underneath.
Q: Can I add a voiceover and keep the original audio?
A: Yes — keep mode on "mix", add the voiceover, and lower the original audio by setting a low volume on additional tracks if you want the voiceover to sit on top.
Q: Can I replace the original audio track?
A: Yes — set mode to "replace" and the original audio is dropped. Only the added tracks are mixed into the output.
Q: What happens if the audio is longer than the video?
A: By default we trim to the video duration. Uncheck "Trim to video duration" if you want the output to extend to the longest input.
Q: Can I adjust the volume of added audio?
A: Yes — each added track has its own volume scalar (0–4×) and a start offset in seconds.
